chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hammad, from Abu Basir, who said:

I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and when he was in the final part of his Tashahhud, he raised his voice so that he made us hear. When he finished, I said, 'Thus it is fitting for the Imam to make his Tashahhud heard by those behind him.' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.تَشَهُّد: Tashahhud, the sitting testimony of faith recited during prayer
key_terms.يُسْمِع: To make heard / to cause to be heard

ai.seo_question: Should the Imam raise his voice during the Tashahhud in congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms the recommended practice (mustahabb) for the Imam to raise his voice during the Tashahhud in congregational prayer, ensuring the followers behind him can hear it. This ruling highlights the importance of communal participation and auditory confirmation in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the Imam's role in leading the congregation through audible recitation of key prayer components.
